Revieve Oy | Senior Product Engineer | REMOTE [Europe / (GMT+2)] | Contract, full-time |

Revieve (Helsinki, with a US office and a team in Asia) builds AI, AR and computer-vision personalization for beauty brands and retailers: skin analysis, virtual try-on and product recommendations. We work with 120+ brands and retailers in 40+ countries, and our product reaches millions of end users.

We're a small team (30+ people, about a dozen engineers) spread across eight time zones, and we've reorganized around the idea that one builder with the right tools can do what a team used to. This role exists because we believe that.

A typical week: a real customer problem lands in front of you with full context, and you decide what to build. Tuesday you sketch it in an AI design tool and prototype in Claude Code. Wednesday it's on staging and you send the founders a Loom. Thursday it's in production. About 1-2 hours of meetings a week, mostly async. No standups, no sprints, no PM or designer in the loop.

What we're looking for:

- Public proof of building: repos, products or side projects we can click around - AI in production, with an opinion about agents, evals, latency and what fails - Fluency with agentic coding (Claude Code, Codex, MCP, custom harnesses) - Design taste: you can take an idea to a working interface without a designer - Generalist instincts: TypeScript/React up front, comfortable with backend integrations and infra - Clear written thinking: READMEs, PRs, post-mortems

Process: intro call, then a paid build session where we work on a real problem together (that's where the hire decision happens, for both sides), a short presentation to the team, then an offer.

Perks: flexible hours, performance-based option plan, equipment budget, five weeks' vacation, paid parental leave.

Details and apply: https://revieve.factorialhr.com/job_posting/senior-product-e... (please mention HN)

Every business with many locations already has systems that record what happened yesterday. None of them tell the manager what to do today. Opaxa does. This is an early, high-intensity role for someone who wants a lot of ownership and to move fast. US work authorization required. No agencies or contract firms.

To apply, email colton@opaxa.com with the subject "Forward Deployed: your name, your city" and include: your resume or LinkedIn; a link to something you built that real people use, and what you personally did on it; two or three sentences on a time a user's feedback changed what you shipped; and where you're based. Mattermost | Remote (US and Canada) | FT | Multiple roles

Mattermost (https://mattermost.com) is an open-core collaboration and workflow automation platform for air-gapped, on-prem and private clouds. Our customers are in defense, intelligence, security and critical infrastructure, including the USAF and NASA. Y Combinator led our Series B, their largest open-source investment at the time.

Both openings are full stack on the core platform: Go backend, React/TypeScript frontend, PostgreSQL and Redis. The codebase is public (https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost), so most of what you build is too. We would rather hire people who ship and own complex software end to end than chase an exact stack match, so any systems or backend language and any frontend stack counts. What we look for in both roles: REST and WebSocket APIs with real networking fundamentals (HTTP, connection lifecycle), and relational databases including schema design and query optimization.

We use coding agents daily (Claude Code, Cursor, and others) at every stage of the work: planning, building, reviewing, testing, and shipping. We treat that as core craft rather than a shortcut around the fundamentals. If you have a track record of shipping and owning complex software end-to-end, we want to hear from you.

Senior Full Stack Engineer $142,723 - $172,723 USD Architect and ship full stack features end to end, own the testing strategy for what you ship, and build internal tooling and testing infrastructure that makes the rest of the team faster. You will work without close supervision and hold the security and compliance bar our customers require. Nice to have: distributed systems and high availability architecture, regulated-environment security, open-source contributions, experience on remote-first teams.

Join our team: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/mattermost/jobs/5379251008

Staff Full Stack Engineer $172,724 - $227,135 USD Set technical direction for the platform rather than for a feature area: architecture and roadmap across the stack, the standards for how the org uses coding agents, and the strategy for internal tooling and testing. You will influence direction across teams, partner with security and compliance on it, and mentor senior engineers. Nice to have: staff, principal or tech lead experience elsewhere, open-source maintainership, FedRAMP or ITAR familiarity, defense or critical infrastructure background.

Join our team: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/mattermost/jobs/5405811008

Both roles have Canadian postings: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/mattermost

Paradromics is building a high bandwidth brain-machine interface for clinical use. The implant we built is restoring function to patients by streaming out neural data from specific brain regions in real time, which we convert to e.g. speech using machine learning. No. That is not what fascism is and using the word like that saps it of all meaning.

This is what Fascism is: [1]

> Fascism (/ˈfæʃɪzəm/ FASH-iz-əm) is a far-right, authoritarian, and ultranationalist political ideology and movement that rose to prominence in early-20th-century Europe.[1][2][3] Fascism is characterized by support for a dictatorial leader, centralized autocracy, militarism, forcible suppression of opposition, belief in a natural social hierarchy, subordination of individual interests for the perceived interest of the nation or race, and strong regimentation of society and the economy

As others have said, one can reasonable debate whether Yarvin should be identified as a fascist or "merely" an authoritarian monarchist. But either way he advocates for the replacement of democracy with an oppressive authoritarian system, is in a position of some influence and power, and is an enemy of anyone who values a free and open society.

If you're not familiar with the Paradox of Tolerance, you should look it up. [2]

> The paradox of tolerance is a philosophical concept suggesting that if a society extends tolerance to those who are intolerant, it risks enabling the eventual dominance of intolerance, thereby undermining the very principle of tolerance.

There is a valid argument to be made that if we want a free, open, and tolerant society we can not tolerate those who publicly argue against that. We don't have to throw them in prison, but they should be "de-platformed" -- boycotted in all public spaces. Their authoritarian ideas discredited and ignored. That's what the parent comment is referring to. And that belief -- that certain ideas that threaten a free, open, and tolerant society should be discredited, de-platformed, and boycotted -- is in no way similar to fascism.

Prior Labs | Berlin, Freiburg, NYC | ONSITE | Full-time | Technical PM, ML Infra, Research Scientist/Engineer, Backend, Full Stack

We build foundation models for tabular data. Deep learning transformed text and images but mostly skipped tables, which are still the data behind most clinical trials, financial models and scientific experiments. The reason is structural: no natural sequence, no spatial structure, no shared vocabulary across datasets, so the architectures and scaling laws behind LLMs don't transfer.

Our approach: pre-train a transformer on millions of synthetic datasets sampled from causal-structure priors. The whole dataset goes in as context, predictions come out in one forward pass. No per-dataset training, no hyperparameter tuning, seconds instead of hours. TabPFN v2 was published in Nature and set a new state of the art; TabPFN-3 scales to 10M rows. 4M+ downloads, 8k+ GitHub stars, in production from liquid biopsy to rail maintenance. Code: https://github.com/PriorLabs/TabPFN

Since July we're an independent lab inside SAP, with more than EUR 1B committed over four years. Models stay open, research stays public, same team and offices.

Roles (most can sit in any of the three offices):

- Technical Product Manager, Integrations: take every model release live across SAP (AI Core to SAP Analytics Cloud), the cloud marketplaces and customer environments, and help decide which channels we build next. Reports to me, close to the code.

- ML Engineer, Infrastructure: own multi-cluster GPU infra (Slurm on GCP today, multi-provider next), training performance and the tooling layer. We spend tens of millions per year on compute; you own that budget.

- Research Scientist, Foundation Model: drive the model agenda - novel architectures, scaling from 10K to 1M+ samples, multimodal and causal directions. PhD plus top-venue publications, or equivalent.

- Research Engineer, Foundation Model: same agenda from the engineering side. You design experiments, write the training and eval infra, and co-author the papers.

- ML Engineer, Backend: design and scale the backend that serves and finetunes the models. Python/FastAPI, Terraform, K8s.

- Full Stack Engineer, ML Platform: build the product end to end. TypeScript + Python, React/FastAPI/Postgres.

Also hiring: Applied Scientist, Forward Deployed ML Engineer, Research Scientist (Foundational Data Science), PhD research interns, plus GTM and ops roles.

40+ people with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Jane Street, Goldman, G-Research, CERN. Led by Frank Hutter, advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Yann LeCun. Comp competitive with top AI labs.

Search Atlas | Product Engineer (Product Manager role, not a Full-stack role) | REMOTE (anywhere, EST hours) | Full-time contractor | $23-$34 USD/hour | https://careers.searchatlas.com/jobs/599248-product-engineer...

We're ~160 people, fully remote, building an AI marketing platform. Our main product is OTTO, which runs a site's SEO on its own - it reads live search data and pushes the technical and on-page fixes itself, nobody queues them up. Around that we've got ad automation for Google and Meta, GBP management for multi-location brands, content gen, and LLM visibility tracking (whether ChatGPT and co are citing you). Autotrader, Hyundai, P&G, Vendasta are some of our customers.

Work happens in pods, 1 PM and 2-4 engineers. You own your pod's roadmap and ship it with them, no veteran PM signing off on your specs first. That's the part most PM roles won't hand you.

Looking for 3+ years PM in B2B SaaS with an actual technical background - eng or QA before PM, or a PM who's been getting into the codebase themselves. You should be able to read Python and TS, write your own SQL, find your way around an API, and not need an engineer to tell you what a stack trace says. We're Django on the back, React/Next on the front. QA is yours end to end including release sign-off, people tend to underestimate that bit. And you're already using Claude Code or similar daily, not "open to it".

A few notes before you apply:

- Experience: we're looking for people with a few years of hands-on product or engineering work behind them. The role is autonomous from the first week, so we need you ready to take the wheel. - Recruiting agencies: we hire in-house and manage every application ourselves, so there's no need to send candidates or reach out about partnerships. Thank you for understanding! - If your stack matches, please do reach out. Django/DRF/Celery/Postgres with React/Next, Python automation work around SEO: if that's your day-to-day and you're using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, whatever you like) in your real workflow, I want to hear from you. Don't talk yourself out of it because the title isn't an exact fit; tell me what you've built.

Recruitment process is screen with me, a take-home that runs about 75 mins, technical round with one of our senior PMs, then a call with our Director of Product (who you'd report to). I usually come back to people within 2 business days.

Our ATS forces us to list specific ywhere as long as you can do EST hours, so apply even if yours isn't

Apply at the link and mention HN somewhere, in your pitch or wherever it fits. joao.pedro@searchatlas.com if you need me, though the link's faster.

P.S: Not a PM, or the PM role isn't quite your thing? Have a look at everything else we have open at https://careers.searchatlas.com and apply directly to the role that suits you best (preferred route). If you're not sure which one that is, email me with a short line on what you do and I'll point you to the right one.
